plan.estimand: 2-level factor main effect in 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA (1 numerator degree of freedom)
plan.hypothesis: Test the main effect of the 2-level factor, fitted model includes all 6 cell means
assumptions: Common variance across all 6 cells (homogeneity of variance)
Balanced design: equal sample size per cell
All 6 cell means fitted in the model
Test uses F-distribution with numerator df=1
missing_information: Specification of the denominator degrees of freedom calculation: total sample size N = 6*n where n = participants per cell, so denominator df = N - 6 = 6n - 6 = 6(n-1). Please confirm this structure is intended.
clarification_questions: The 3-by-2 factorial has 6 cells with n participants each, yielding N = 6n total participants. When all 6 cell means are fitted, the model has 6 parameters, leaving denominator df = N - 6. Is this the intended design structure?
Partial η² = 0.06 is the effect size for the 2-level factor main effect. Should I assume this is computed as F_effect / (F_effect + F_error) using the numerator F-statistic and error MS?
Is the test two-sided (α = 0.05 total) as standard, or do you require one-sided?
Should I use the noncentrality parameter λ = (partial η² / (1 - partial η²)) × denominator_df, then compute power via the noncentral F-distribution?
scientific_notes: Partial η² = 0.06 is a small-to-medium effect in the factorial ANOVA context.
With denominator df = 6(n-1), the noncentrality λ depends on n nonlinearly, requiring iterative solution or tabular lookup for target power.
The conversion from partial η² to noncentrality λ assumes the focal effect and error are independent in the expected MS structure.
